problem:
If the point $P$ has polar coordinates $(2,{300}^{∘}),$ then its Cartesian coordinates are

$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
worked_solution:
To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡({300}^{∘}) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡({300}^{∘}) \\  & =2(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(1,-\sqrt{3}).$
